name: Moana Surfrider, a Westin Resort
positioning: Historic beachfront resort on Waikiki Beach, the first hotel on Waikiki (officially Moana Surfrider, A Westin Resort & Spa, Waikiki Beach)
best_for: Travelers who want history and a beachfront setting on Waikiki
Families interested in hula, ukulele and lei-making activities

facts.text: The Moana Surfrider opened in 1901 as the first hotel on Waikiki Beach.
The Historic Banyan Wing honors architect Oliver G. Traphagen's original 1901 design, including its Beaux-Arts detailing.
Tower Wing rooms have a built-in reading nook and a deep lanai that opens the room to Pacific Ocean breezes.
The Surfrider Wing has a contemporary design drawn from surf culture, and its oceanfront rooms have rocking chairs with Pacific views.
The resort has a beachfront stretch of over 600 feet on Waikiki Beach.
The spa has a whirlpool spa, dry and wet saunas, private relaxation rooms and couples suites.
Complimentary activities include Storytelling with Tutu, wellness classes, ukulele and hula lessons, and lei making.
The resort runs historical tours about the history of the First Lady of Waikiki.
The Veranda's breakfast buffet includes Japanese breakfast selections and mochi waffles.
Guests can take surf and outrigger canoeing lessons.

highlights.text: The Banyan Tree, named Deva, is 75 feet high, stretches 150 feet across and is a millennium landmark tree.
The beachfront pool is set beneath the Banyan Tree.
Moana Lani Spa's treatments draw on Hawaiian healing practice and include massage, body treatments, facials and nail services.
Carved wooden Moana rocking chairs line the Kalakaua Avenue-facing veranda.
Afternoon Tea is served on the Veranda with oceanfront views.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the historic building may have smaller rooms than newer resorts.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing due to the beachfront location and historic significance.
